outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome in this isolated pair: the current completed status evaluations show both parallel and serial failed 0 of 4 official tests. The concrete task-solving difference is process and closure quality: serial used a single upstream-porting path and ended with final local verification, while parallel used seven live children, absorbed shared-workspace instability, made late runner edits, and timed out before final closure. These parallel patterns are adverse, but the mounted evidence does not prove that they caused a different official result because the serial control also failed.
parallel_contributors: Seven-way fan-out plus parent reconciliation exhausted the available closure budget.
Post-verification runner edits were not followed by a completed final full verification loop.
Live shared workspace writes made package imports fail while sibling modules were still absent.
serial_contributors: Single actor used the matching upstream project and sequenced integration before final verification.
Serial completed local tests, spec examples, install checks, cleanup, and final response without timeout.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel wrote more bespoke component and test code and later added mask-scaling fixes; serial ported more directly from the upstream repository.
Both artifacts satisfied local checks reported in the trajectory but still failed the hidden official evaluator.
evaluator_effects: Only aggregate official counts are mounted; the specific hidden testcase failures are not available inside the allowed pair inputs.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: parallel adverse process patterns with no official outcome difference
